source_text: This effect stems from removing the foreskin, which can accumulate smegma, foster chronic inflammation, and enable human papillomavirus (HPV) persistence—cofactors in penile carcinogenesis—as indicated by lower HPV prevalence (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.46–0.70) in circumcised men. [106] [5]
